source: Clark & Luce 1965, 'Intensities of Orchestral Instrument Scales Played at Prescribed Dynamic Markings', J. Audio Eng. Soc. 13(2) 151-157, Fig. 2: each instrument's average level of chromatic scales played pp / mf / ff 'as in typical orchestral music' (two players, with and without vibrato), dB SPL re 20 uPa at 10 m in the instrument's loudest direction (anechoic, inverse-square to 10 m). Read from the 300 dpi scan by pixel position (ticks 40..80 dB, 14.39 px/dB; the bar caps' and the dot's centres); each bar's ff - pp agrees with the printed Table I dynamic range within 0.3 dB (tableI). Review page: https://claude.ai/artifact/67i6bLfUGkfrkLVLWQdT2e
directivity: diMax: directivity index (dB) in the instrument's loudest direction, derived from TU Berlin's single-tone directivities (Ackermann, Boehm, Brinkmann & Weinzierl, TU Berlin, 1a_DirectivitiesSingleTones_SOFA, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; derived numbers only): RMS pressure at 32 receivers on a 2.06 m sphere, ff, steady part; DI_r = L_r - 10 log10(sum w_r p_r^2), spherical Voronoi weights; one receiver per instrument, the one with the highest mean DI over its notes (Clark & Luce kept one mic direction per instrument); diNotes notes
